plain_english: Now indirect initiation is twofold: the dead one, and the jīva-part.
sanskrit_cite: atha parokṣasya dīkṣā dvividhaś ca saḥ mṛto jīvaṃś ca

plain_english: Therein [the command]: one who has served the guru — whether dead, or banished, or killed by sorcery and the rest, or killed as an infant, or arisen at the death-moment as willed, or one whose power-descent has come through another mouth — or likewise one to be initiated: such is the command.
sanskrit_cite: tatra kṛtaguruseva eva mṛta udvāsito vā abhicārādihato ḍimbāhato mṛtyukṣaṇoditatathāruciḥ mukhāntarāyātaśaktipāto vā tathā dīkṣya ity ājñā

plain_english: And in the dead-initiation, adhivāsa-and-rest is not used.
sanskrit_cite: atra ca mṛtadīkṣāyām adhivāsādi na upayujyate

plain_english: In the mandala — where abundant rite, the supreme instrument, flower-and-rest seat, pedestal-and-rest mandala, trident-lotus-and-rest form, the specific meditation-object mantra, itself radiant — of the meditation-devoted yogi, of him rich in one-devotion-immersion, and of the knower: these are the presence-causes, stated in order.
sanskrit_cite: maṇḍale mantraviśeṣasaṃnidhaye yatra bahulā kriyā uttamam upakaraṇaṃ puṣpādi sthānaṃ pīṭhādi maṇḍalaṃ triśūlābjādi ākṛtiḥ dhyeyaviśeṣaḥ mantraḥ svayaṃ dīptaś ca dhyānaparasya yoginaḥ tadekabhaktisamāveśaśālino jñāninaś ca sambandhaḥ ity ete saṃnidhānahetavo yathottaram uktāḥ

plain_english: In their conjunction, what talk would there be? — thus it was said by the Supreme Lord.
sanskrit_cite: samuditatve tu kā kathā syāt iti parameśvareṇa uktam

plain_english: Then, having worshipped the god and established his kuśa-and-rest form in front, by the guru-derived order of knowledge-teaching let him see it; and he, rising from the muladhara, having crossed by seminal power the spread-out endless nerve-path-staff to the nose-sky, scattering — let him seek to pervade.
sanskrit_cite: tato devaṃ pūjayitvā tadākṛtiṃ kuśādimayīm agre sthāpayitvā gurvāsāditajñānopadeśakrameṇa tāṃ paśyet sa ca mūlādhārād udetya prasṛtasuvitatānantanāḍyadhvadaṇḍaṃ vīryeṇākramya nāsāgaganaparigataṃ vikṣipan vyāptum īṣṭe

plain_english: As long as, by smoke favorably heaped in fine-flame mesh, the path-wheel is covered and the desired jīva is brought in — thus the great jala-named practice.
sanskrit_cite: yāvad dhūmābhirāmapracitataraśikhājālakenādhvacakraṃ saṃchādyābhīṣṭajīvānayanam iti mahāñ jālanāmā prayogaḥ

plain_english: By this, the to-be-covered goes into another's power — facing first; afterwards the whole is brought, if — or then even from the path's middle, as he wishes.
sanskrit_cite: etenācchādanīyaṃ vrajati paravaśaṃ saṃmukhīnatvam ādau paścād ānīyate cet sakalam atha tato 'py adhvamadhyād yatheṣṭam

plain_english: Two-drawn or two-raised, or within a dead person's scope, that-which-is-to-be-drawn in the jīva: the yoga gone through blessed Śaṃbhunātha's tradition — jala-named, told by me.
sanskrit_cite: ākṛṣṭāv uddhatau vā mṛtajanaviṣaye karṣaṇīye 'tha jīve yogaḥ śrīśaṃbhunāthāgamaparigamito jālanāmā mayoktaḥ

plain_english: Outside too — thus how does it not happen, from drawing-and-rest without practice, if asked: by passion, hatred and the rest yoked, in its operation, from the aiśvarya-immersion yoke.
sanskrit_cite: bahir api itthaṃ kathaṃ na bhavati ākarṣaṇādau vinābhyāsāt iti cet rāgadveṣādiyogavaśena tatpravṛttau aiśvaryāveśāyogāt

plain_english: Then, from being necessarily controlled, dependence on practice-and-rest would indeed be.
sanskrit_cite: tato niyatiniyantritatvāt abhyāsādyapekṣā syād eva

plain_english: Here, however, from immersion in grace-natured Lordhood, such is the state.
sanskrit_cite: iha tu anugrahātmakaparameśvaratāveśāt tathābhāvaḥ

plain_english: For the Supreme Lord himself, by the door of the guru's body-abode, graces those to be graced.
sanskrit_cite: parameśvara eva hi guruśarīrādhiṣṭhānadvāreṇa anugrāhyān anugṛhṇāti

plain_english: And he, of unthinkable glory — it is mostly said.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca acintyamahimā iti uktaprāyam

plain_english: Thus drawn by the jala-practice, the jīva, having entered dārbha, jasmine-fruit-and-rest or the body, becomes; nor does he tremble, from the absence of mind-breath-and-rest equipment; but by the force of that contemplation he trembles even so — as before: the purification-and-rest consecration, within the full-offering's yojana-end.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ jālaprayogākṛṣṭo jīvo dārbhaṃ jātīphalādi vā śarīraṃ samāviṣṭo bhavati na ca spandate manaḥpraṇādisāmagryabhāvāt tadanudhyānabalāt tu spandate 'pi tādṛśe 'pi tasmin pūrvavat prokṣaṇādisaṃskāraḥ pūrṇāhutiyojanikāntaḥ

plain_english: Here, further, by the full-offering, dissolution of the dārbha-and-rest form in the supreme fire is to be done.
sanskrit_cite: atra paraṃ pūrṇāhutyā tasya dārbhādyākārasya paratejasi layaḥ kartavyaḥ

plain_english: Thus raised out, he is released by the full-offering itself — if he stands in the hell-ghost-animal classes.
sanskrit_cite: evam uddhṛto 'sau pūrṇāhutyaiva apavṛjyate yadi svarnarakapretatiryakṣu sthitaḥ

plain_english: A man, just then, obtains knowledge, yoga, initiation, or discernment.
sanskrit_cite: manuṣyas tu tadaiva jñānaṃ yogaṃ dīkṣāṃ vivekaṃ vā labhate

plain_english: From being an eligible body — thus the raising-of-the-dead.
sanskrit_cite: adhikāriśarīratvāt iti mṛtoddharaṇam

plain_english: Even for the living, in indirect [initiation], when power-descent arises: this very sequence — excepting the dārbha-form-imagination jīva-drawing.
sanskrit_cite: jīvato 'pi parokṣasya utpanne śaktipāte 'yam eva kramaḥ dārbhākṛtikalpanajīvākṛṣṭivarjam

plain_english: The consecration of the one established by mere meditation itself.
sanskrit_cite: dhyānamātropasthāpitasyaiva asya saṃskāraḥ

plain_english: Initiation gives both the enjoyment and the enjoyer.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣā ca bhogabhokṣobhayadāyinī

plain_english: From the strength of one's own habit, and the unthinkability of severing the enjoyment-habit: by many, in initiation, the higher-doctrine consecration is strong; another would be for that consecration.
sanskrit_cite: svavāsanābalīyastvāt bhogavāsanāvicchedasya ca asaṃbhāvyamānatvāt bahubhiḥ dīkṣāyām ūrdhvaśāsanasaṃskāro balavān anyas tu tatsaṃskārāya syāt

plain_english: Likewise for the initiated from outside — the manifestation of knowledge-and-rest, it is said.
sanskrit_cite: paroṣasyāpi dīkṣitasya tathaiva jñānādyāvirbhāvaḥ iti
